core_obligations: Test on an acyclic complex (proof lines 8798-8806): for an acyclic complex K^bullet of O-modules, compute Hom_{K(O)}(K^bullet, SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet, I^bullet)) by the four-term displayed chain.

Identify the terms (proof lines 8807-8820): the first equality is the global-cohomology description, the second is the composition lemma rewriting the internal hom into an internal hom as the internal hom from the total tensor product, and the third is the global-cohomology description again.

Conclude vanishing (proof lines 8821-8826): the last term is Hom_{K(O)}(Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet), I^bullet), which is zero because Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet) is acyclic — the tensor product of an acyclic complex with a K-flat complex being acyclic by definition of K-flatness — and I^bullet is K-injective; hence the internal hom complex is K-injective.
proof_roadmap: Show that every acyclic complex has no homotopy classes of maps into the internal hom complex.
Rewrite the Hom group through the global cohomology equation and the composition lemma as a Hom into the K-injective complex from a total tensor product.
Use K-flatness to see that total tensor product is acyclic and K-injectivity to conclude it vanishes.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the internal hom from a K-flat complex into a K-injective complex is K-injective (statement lines 8788-8795). The proof (proof lines 8797-8826) is a four-term computation of the homotopy Hom group out of an acyclic complex: the global-cohomology equation and the composition lemma rewrite it as a Hom into the K-injective complex from Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet), which is acyclic because L^bullet is K-flat, so the group vanishes. H2: one computation with two identifications, written out.
